dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5301.text: Adornment. Formed from 衣, with 象 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5302.text: The clothing regularly worn each day. Formed from 衣 and 日; 日 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5303.text: Private clothing. Formed from 衣, with 埶 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “This is a private garment.”

shuowen:5304.text: An inner, private garment. Formed from 衣, with 中 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “All wore their everyday clothes inside.”

shuowen:5305.text: Fine and beautiful. Formed from 衣, with 朱 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The quiet girl is lovely.”

shuowen:5306.text: An affair being good or pleasing. Formed from 衣, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5307.text: To join on and add. Formed from 衣, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5308.text: Without color. Formed from 衣, with 半 indicating the sound. Another explanation cites the Odes: “This is a 紲袢 garment.” Read like 普.

shuowen:5309.text: The five colors coming together. Formed from 衣, with 集 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5310.text: Abundance of clothing and goods. Formed from 衣, with 谷 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “With sincerity, there is abundance and no blame.”

shuowen:5311.text: To fold clothing. Formed from 衣, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5312.text: To rub and spread clothing smooth. Formed from 衣, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5313.text: Remnants of silk fabric. Formed from 衣, with 𠛱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5314.text: Worn clothing. Formed from 衣, with 奴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5315.text: A garment’s seams coming undone. Formed from 衣, with 旦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5316.text: To make clothing whole. Formed from 衣, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5317.text: To stitch clothing. Formed from 衣 and 黹; 黹 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5318.text: To strip away clothing. Formed from 衣, with 虒 indicating the sound. Read like 池.

shuowen:5319.text: To bare oneself. Formed from 衣, with 𣎆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5320.text: To bare oneself. Formed from 衣, with 呈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5321.text: To bare oneself. Formed from 衣, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5322.text: Crooked or improper, 𠆎. Formed from 衣, with 牙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5323.text: To gather things in the front fold of one’s garment is 襭. Formed from 衣, with 頡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5324.text: Holding up the garment’s front fold is 袺. Formed from 衣, with 吉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5325.text: The garment 帴. Formed from 衣, with 曹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5326.text: To wrap. Formed from 衣, with 壯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5327.text: To wind around. Formed from 衣, with 果 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5328.text: A book bag. Formed from 衣, with 邑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5329.text: A seam or stitched edge, 緶. Formed from 衣, with 齊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5330.text: A long hemp jacket worn by servants. Formed from 衣, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5331.text: Clothing woven from hemp. Formed from 衣, with 區 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a head wrap. Another: a cloth wrapped to catch saliva.

shuowen:5332.text: Stockings woven from hemp. Another explanation: coarse clothing. Formed from 衣, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5333.text: The collar of a 䙔 garment. Formed from 衣, with 匽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5334.text: A 褗 collar is called 裺. Formed from 衣, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5335.text: A rain garment of grass, called 萆 in Qin. Formed from 衣; pictographic.

shuowen:5336.text: The clothing of serving bondservants is called 卒: clothing bearing identifying marks.

shuowen:5337.text: A servant’s marked garment, 卒. Formed from 衣, with 者 indicating the sound. Another explanation: making clothes.

shuowen:5338.text: To cut out. Formed from 衣 and 制.

shuowen:5339.text: Clothing of the Man and Yi peoples. Formed from 衣, with 犮 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a knee covering.

shuowen:5340.text: To clothe the dead. Formed from 衣, with 遂 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Chu made the duke personally clothe the corpse.”

shuowen:5341.text: The fine-silk lining inside a coffin. Formed from 衣 and 弔. Read like 雕.

shuowen:5342.text: Clothes and coverings presented for the dead are called 裞. Formed from 衣, with 兌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5343.text: A spirit’s clothing. Formed from 衣, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound. Read like 縈 in the Odes’ “Kudzu and vines wind around it”; alternatively like 袾 in “The quiet girl is lovely.”

shuowen:5344.text: A carriage’s warm covering. Formed from 衣, with 延 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5345.text: To lead or tie a horse with a woven cord. Formed from 衣 and 馬.

shuowen:5346.text: Full ceremonial dress. Formed from 衣, with 玄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5347.text: A garment. Formed from 衣, with 彡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5348.text: A kind of fur garment. Formed from 衣, with 奥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5349.text: A hide garment. Formed from 衣, with 求 indicating the sound. Another explanation: pictographic, using the same principle as 衰. All characters in this group are formed from 裘.

shuowen:5350.text: The lining of a fur garment. Formed from 裘, with 鬲 indicating the sound. Read like 擊.

shuowen:5351.text: Old. Seventy years is called 老. Formed from 人, 毛 and 匕, indicating beard and hair turning white. All characters in this group are formed from 老.

shuowen:5352.text: Eighty years of age is called 耊. Formed from abbreviated 老 and 至.

shuowen:5353.text: Ninety years of age is called 𦽡. Formed from 老 and abbreviated 蒿.

shuowen:5354.text: Old. Formed from abbreviated 老, with 旨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5355.text: An old person’s face dark and mottled as if dirty; the wording 凍黎 is uncertain. Formed from abbreviated 老, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5356.text: An old person’s face appearing spotted. Formed from abbreviated 老, with 占 indicating the sound. Read like 耿 in 耿介.

shuowen:5357.text: An old person walking, the steps barely keeping up. Formed from abbreviated 老 and abbreviated 易, depicting walking. Read like 樹.

shuowen:5358.text: Long-lasting. Formed from abbreviated 老, with 𠷎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5359.text: Old. Formed from abbreviated 老, with 丂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5360.text: Serving one’s parents well. Formed from abbreviated 老 and 子; the child supports the old.

shuowen:5361.text: Eyebrows, hair and the like, and animal hair. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 毛.

shuowen:5362.text: Hair abundant. Formed from 毛, with 隼 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Birds and beasts have rich coats.”

shuowen:5363.text: The coarse hairs of beasts. Formed from 毛, with 倝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5364.text: In mid-autumn, birds’ and beasts’ coats are abundant and can be selected for making useful objects. Formed from 毛, with 先 indicating the sound. Read like 選.

shuowen:5365.text: A woolen cloth whose color resembles 虋, hence called 𣯩. 虋 is a cereal’s red shoots. Formed from 毛, with 㒼 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Woolen robes like 𣯩.”

shuowen:5366.text: Rolled or compressed wool. Formed from 毛, with 亶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5367.text: Feather or hair ornaments. Formed from 毛, with 耳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5368.text: 氍毹 and 毾㲪 are kinds of felt and woolen cloth, apparently regional names. Formed from 毛, with 瞿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5369.text: The woolen fabric 氍毹. Formed from 毛, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5370.text: The woolen fabric 毾㲪. Formed from 毛, with 𦐇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5371.text: The woolen fabric 毾㲪. Formed from 毛, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5372.text: A round leather ball. Formed from 毛, with 求 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5373.text: Split bird feathers used for banners and great standards. Formed from 毛, with 敞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5374.text: Fine animal hair. Formed from three 毛. All characters in this group are formed from 毳.

shuowen:5375.text: Hair in a tangle. Formed from 毳, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5376.text: To lay out. Depicts lying down. All characters in this group are formed from 尸.

shuowen:5377.text: To keep ready or reserve. Formed from 尸, with 奠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5378.text: To squat. Formed from 尸 and 古; 居 follows 古.

shuowen:5379.text: To lie down and rest. Formed from 尸 and 自.

shuowen:5380.text: Urgent, insistent movements. Formed from 尸, with 䏌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5381.text: To turn. Formed from 尸, with abbreviated 𧝑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5382.text: Walking with difficulty. Another explanation: the utmost limit. Formed from 尸, with 凷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5383.text: The buttocks, 𦞠. Formed from 尸, with 九 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5384.text: The thigh. Formed beneath 尸, with 丌 resting on 几; the graphical wording is uncertain.

shuowen:5385.text: The buttocks. Formed from 尸, with 旨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5386.text: To approach from behind. Formed from 尸, with 匕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5387.text: To insert or crowd in from behind. Formed from 尸 and 臿.

shuowen:5388.text: Crowding in, 㞚㞏. Formed from 尸, with 乏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5389.text: To soften hide. Formed by extending behind 尸; some forms use 又 for 尸. The graphical explanation is uncertain.

shuowen:5390.text: A prostrate appearance. Formed from 尸, with 辰 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a roof or eaves.

shuowen:5391.text: Lingering or slow, 屖遟. Formed from 尸, with 辛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5392.text: Footwear. Formed from 尸, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5393.text: The principal remains at death. Formed from 尸 and 死.

shuowen:5394.text: To cut open. Formed from 尸, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5395.text: A lining inside footwear. Formed from 尸, with 枼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5396.text: A dwelling. Formed from 尸, the one who occupies it. Another explanation: 尸 depicts a building. It also uses 至, the place one reaches and stops. Both 室 and 屋 follow 至.

shuowen:5397.text: To screen or conceal. Formed from 尸, with 幷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5398.text: A building with multiple stories. Formed from 尸, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5399.text: Repeatedly. Note: the present 婁 was originally the character in 屢空; this graph was added by later people. Formed from 尸; further details are unknown.

shuowen:5400.text: Ten cun. On the human hand, the moving pulse ten divisions back forms the cun-opening; ten cun make one chi. Chi is used to indicate measures and regulate affairs. Formed from 尸 and 乙; 乙 is the marker. Under Zhou, cun, chi, zhi, xun, chang, ren and other measures all took the human body as their standard. All characters in this group are formed from 尺. The anatomical wording is uncertain.
